featured_reviews.name: Noor Sayeed Khan
featured_reviews.review_text:
Madras Diaries in Bandra has such a gorgeous, welcoming vibe, it’s easily one of the prettiest spots for South Indian food in the city. The staff was genuinely sweet and the service was so smooth it made the whole experience feel really relaxed.

We decided to try their new chaat menu, and the Shakkarkand Matar ki Chaat was a total winner, it felt super fresh and not at all oily. The Chatpata Singhada (water chestnut) was a fun surprise too, especially for that unique crunch you don't usually find in street food.

The Madras Diaries Special Combo is a solid choice if you’re like me and can't decide the medu vada was perfectly crispy. But honestly, the real highlight was the Filter Coffee with those Rawa Biscuits. It’s such a nostalgic, comforting pairing. We finished with the Elaneer Payasum, which was light and refreshing, though I wish there was just a bit more of it! Definitely worth a visit if you’re in Bandra and want a meal that feels both clean and satisfying.

featured_reviews.name: Allen Samuel
featured_reviews.review_text:
Madras Diaries is a perfect blend of authentic South Indian comfort and exciting new flavours! The highlight now is their chaat menu, which adds a fun, chatpata twist alongside their classic offerings.

The Chatpata Singhada and Shakkarkand Matar Ki Chaat were vibrant, tangy, and full of flavour. The Chettinad Paneer with flaky wheat parotta was rich and satisfying, paired beautifully with the soft Kodumai (wheat) parotta. Refreshing sips like the Cold Coffee and Virgin Mojito balanced the meal, while the Elaneer Payasam was a light, delicious finish.

The presentation of each dish was impressive and clearly made with attention to detail. Service was warm and prompt, making the overall experience even more enjoyable.

With its warm décor and relaxed, inviting ambience, Madras Diaries is a must-visit for a wholesome meal with a unique chaat twist!

featured_reviews.name: Aaniket R Naddkarni

VARUGA VARUGA ❤️

Everyone is craving South Indian food these days… looks like Idli & Dosa have officially become Gen Z’s favorite comfort food 😍
So we decided to check out Madras Diaries in Bandra — a place already famous for authentic South Indian food, but now they’ve also launched CHATS… and trust me, this will make you visit again & again!

Without wasting any time, we started with our favorite — Pani Puri 🤤
And bhai sahab… they served it with 3 different flavor waters — Mumbai style, Delhiwala & Kolkata style!
We literally couldn’t stop eating 😅

Then came the Palak Patta Chaat…
And bhai, ekdum Delhi ki yaad dila di ❤️

To beat the summer heat, we tried their Kokum Cooler & Mint Cooler — super refreshing and fresh!

For mains, we ordered Mini Idlies served with 4 different chutneys… and trust me, this combo is something you’ll only get here, so make sure it’s on your order list ✔️

We also tried the Malabar Paratha with Chettinad Paneer — great quantity, rich flavors, and the paneer was super soft 😍

And finally in desserts, Pineapple Sheera… simple, comforting, and honestly made with love ❤️
So make sure you visit Madras Diaries

featured_reviews.name: Vinay Pasi
featured_reviews.review_text:
Visited Mutuswami Cafe in Khar and really enjoyed the overall experience. The place has a simple, casual vibe but serves a wide variety of dishes—from authentic South Indian options to Mumbai street-style favourites.

The benne dosa stood out with its crispy texture and buttery flavour, while the idli was soft and fresh. The cheese pav bhaji and mushroom sukha combo added a nice desi touch to the meal. The mango milkshake and mango sheera were rich, sweet, and perfect to end on a high note.

Service was quick, though it can get a bit crowded during peak hours. Overall, it’s a great place for breakfast or a casual meal with good food and decent pricing. Would definitely visit again.

featured_reviews.review_text:
Absolutely loved my experience at muttuswami Khar🌟
Started with the refreshing Kala Khatta and Aam Panna coolers — both were perfect for the Mumbai heat. The Ghee Podi Idli was super soft and flavourful, while the Masala Benne Dosa was buttery, crisp and delicious. For mains, the Ghee Roast Mushroom with Appam and Chettinad Biryani were packed with authentic flavours and tasted amazing. Ended the meal with Payasam and Vanilla Gelato which made for the perfect dessert combo. Great food, comforting flavours and an overall amazing dining experience. Highly recommended!

featured_reviews.name: Mahima Pal
featured_reviews.review_text:
Visited the Khar outlet recently and absolutely loved the whole experience 🫶🏻

The café has such a warm and cozy vibe with a perfect blend of authentic South Indian flavours and modern café aesthetics. Every dish felt comforting, flavourful, and beautifully prepared.

We started with the Cheese Onion Uttappa which was soft, perfectly cooked, and loaded with cheese without overpowering the authentic taste. The Mutuswami Special Benne Dosa with paneer was honestly one of the highlights 🤤 crispy on the outside, buttery, rich, and filled generously with flavourful paneer stuffing.

The Ghee Roast Mushroom with Appam was another standout dish. The appams were soft and fluffy while the mushroom preparation had a beautiful spicy South Indian flavour that paired so well together. We also tried the Paneer Cheese Grilled Sandwich which was super cheesy, crisp, and comforting.

For drinks, the Chikoo Milkshake was thick, creamy, and refreshing, while the Kala Khatta Cooler from their summer specials was tangy, nostalgic, and perfect for the Mumbai heat.
Ended the meal with Mango Sheera and it was the sweetest ending possible 🤌🏻 warm, rich, and full of mango flavour without being overly sweet.

Loved the quality, presentation, ambience, and overall experience. Definitely a place I’d love visiting again for comforting South Indian food with a modern twist.

featured_reviews.review_text:
Mutuswami is one of those simple, comforting south indian food places which serve superb food. Calm and relaxed vibe - no rush, no noise just pure happiness. I went to Muttuswami Café with my skeptical, firang partner. He loved it, and so did I.

We had the Muttuswamy Special Benne Dosa, which is a mix of Benne Dosa, Masala Dosa and Ghee Podi Dosa. We also had Idli Vada Rasam, Plain and Hazelnut Filter Coffee, and a Pineapple Sheera to top it off. All of it was delicious, as well as pleasing to the eye!

The restaurant has been done up beautifully - it feels like you're walking into another world. It's super clean, and all the little touches - from the dabbara set for the filter coffee, to the paan box for the mukhwaas - serve to further elevate the experience.

Special thanks to Gaurav for being so patient and helpful.

featured_reviews.review_text: There’s a new South Indian food spot in the city so I had to check it out. Nanna House in Bandra is serving Andhra style food and I tried their specials. featured_reviews.name: sucheta thakur
featured_reviews.review_text:
If there’s one place Bandra needs to start forming lines for, it’s @nannahouseindia on 16th Road. This Andhra-style spot is all set to change the way Bandra — actually, Bombay — experiences South Indian food. And yes, maybe it sounds like I’m exaggerating… but one meal here is enough to prove why I’m not.

From the moment the food arrived, everything reminded me of the kind of flavours that feel simple, comforting, yet absolutely unforgettable.

We started with the Pesarattu, beautifully stuffed with upma — a combination that instantly transported me back to Hyderabad. The texture, the seasoning, the warmth… it just hits in the most nostalgic way.

Next up was the star of the show: the Butter Masala Dosa. Cooked in Amul butter and finished with a generous dollop of white butter, this dosa is easily one of the best in Bombay. Crisp edges, a soft centre, flavour-packed masala — truly dosa heaven.

The Butter Podi Idli followed the same theme — soft idlis coated in podi and topped with white butter. Comforting, buttery, and delicious in every bite.

And of course, no South Indian meal is complete without Filter Coffee. Their version is strong, aromatic, and balanced — exactly how a proper filter coffee should be.

But the surprise winner? The Filter Coffee Soft Serve. Smooth, perfectly sweet, full of coffee flavour — honestly, the perfect end to this meal. I’d go back just for this. ❤️

In a city overflowing with restaurants, Nanna House India stands out for its authenticity, warmth, and flavour-packed dishes. What are you waiting for? This is the place Bandra needs queues for — and trust me, once you try it, you’ll understand why.

The millet cone idlis were soft and wholesome, and the podi idlis had the perfect balance of ghee and spice.

Add a cup of traditional filter coffee and the experience feels complete. Highly recommended for anyone looking for the best Andhra restaurant in Bandra.

The decor and overall aesthetic of this place are truly beautiful. The ambiance, design, and attention to detail make it feel like a high-end spot, and walking in, you definitely expect a premium dining experience. Unfortunately, while the space looks stunning, the actual experience did not live up to the expectations, especially considering the reputation and standard one would associate with a place like this.

The biggest issue by far was the number of bugs. There were so many insects flying around our table while we were eating, which completely ruined the experience. What made it even more uncomfortable was that the staff were actively killing bugs right next to us as we were dining, which felt extremely unhygienic and honestly quite disgusting. It completely took away from the enjoyment of the meal and made it hard to relax or even finish our food comfortably. For a restaurant of this level, this is simply unacceptable and needs serious attention.

In terms of the food, it was a mixed experience. The watermelon and pineapple juices were good — fresh, refreshing, and nicely prepared. The watermelon salad, however, lacked flavor and felt quite underwhelming, especially given how promising it sounded on the menu.

We ordered the edamame peas and the spicy chicken, and those dishes were actually quite good. They were well-cooked, flavorful, and enjoyable, which showed that the kitchen does have potential. However, good dishes alone cannot make up for poor hygiene standards and an uncomfortable dining environment.

The service also felt below expectation. It didn’t reflect the quality, attentiveness, or polish you would normally associate with a Bastian-level standard. Overall, the experience felt disorganized and lacking in the fine-dining attention to detail that one would expect.

In summary, while the decor is stunning and some of the food items were good, the bug issue and service quality seriously impacted the experience. It did not feel like a Bastian-standard restaurant, and until these issues are resolved, it’s hard to recommend. With better hygiene control, improved service, and more consistency in food quality, this place could truly live up to its potential — but for now, it unfortunately falls short.

featured_reviews.review_text:
This place by the Bawa Hotels Group is a good option if you’re in the mood for Punjabi food, just don’t walk in expecting completely authentic flavours. The taste is slightly toned down, but if you set your expectations right, you’ll actually enjoy the food.

The menu is quite well done, and the meal box options are a big plus. Makes ordering super easy without having to overthink or pick too many individual items.

Their parathas are definitely worth trying—served nicely with curd. Do ask for white butter separately though, as it’s not given by default and really makes a difference. The lassi is a must-have here, easily one of the better things on the menu.

Also, a special mention for the Kalimiri chicken shorba. It’s not on the menu, but if they have it, don’t miss it—it’s genuinely very good.

Ambience is nice and comfortable, so no complaints there. Service, however, is quite slow and needs serious improvement, which can get a bit frustrating.

Parking is another issue—since it’s close to the railway station, the area is always crowded and finding a spot is tough. Better to plan that in advance.

Overall, a good place to chill and enjoy a meal, as long as you’re okay overlooking the service and parking hassles.

**“Extremely disappointing and mentally frustrating experience. I ordered 2 Masala Dosa and 2 boxes of Medu Wada (each box containing 4 pieces, around ₹211 each), along with a watermelon juice add-on.

Shockingly, I did not receive the Medu Wada at all. I only received 2 boxes containing Masala Dosa with chutney and sambhar.

When I contacted the restaurant, they first told me to check properly and said there should be 3 boxes. After confirming with their kitchen, they firmly stated that everything was packed and sent correctly. Then they shifted the responsibility, saying if anything happens during transit, it is Zomato and the delivery partner’s issue.

But this is where the real problem lies. Instead of taking accountability or properly investigating, responsibility is being passed around. This creates a system where no one is answerable, and the only person who suffers is the customer who paid honestly.

Also, blaming the delivery stage so casually makes no sense. A delivery partner is not just a middle person—they are the backbone of this entire system. Without them, restaurants cannot deliver food and platforms cannot function. Indirectly shifting blame without clarity or resolution only reflects poor coordination and lack of accountability in the entire process.

In the end, both the restaurant and Zomato get paid, but the customer is left with incomplete food, no proper explanation, no immediate support, and only different excuses from everyone involved.

This is not just about a missing item, it reflects a deeper issue of responsibility, coordination, and customer respect. Very irresponsible service and a truly disappointing experience.”**

“If the system cannot ensure accountability, then the customer will always be the weakest and most ignored part of it.”

featured_reviews.name: Nikhil Kamath
featured_reviews.review_text:
Tried Shankar Mahadevan’s @malgudi.ind in Chembur during my recent Mumbai trip, a restaurant that’s become quite popular for its modern take on South Indian food. We started with the Anna Style Crispy Lotus Root, which had a tangy tamarind-heavy flavour and worked well as a snack. The much-hyped Mulbagal Dosa, though visually interesting with its parcel-like shape, tasted fairly ordinary. The Davangere Benne Podi Dosa followed a similar route, comforting but not very memorable beyond the podi and butter.

For the main course, we ordered Sanchi’s Vegetable Stew with Appam and Veg Malabar Curry with Malabar Parotta. The curry and parotta were satisfying, but the stew felt too watery and lacked the comforting richness you expect from a good appam-stew combination.

The real standout was the Filter Kaapi Panna Cotta. Smooth, creamy, and packed with coffee and jaggery flavour, it easily ended up being the best thing on the table.

featured_reviews.name: Mridula Bhat

What stands out is how they’ve retained the comfort of familiar flavours while introducing thoughtful, modern elements, especially in their coffee menu. The filter coffee variations are genuinely interesting.

The space itself has a warm, slightly nostalgic vibe.

Food quality was solid. Service was courteous.

We highly recommend Ghee Podi Thatthe Idli, Mulbagal Dosa, Mushroom Ghee Roast with Neer Dosa, Sri Lankan Tamil Curry with Idiyappam, Bisi Bele Bhaath and the soulful and delicious Sheera for dessert.

For drinks, we tried Mango Matcha Beery and Iced Kaapi (this had jaggery and ghee) and was delicious!

Overall, it’s a place worth visiting if you’re looking to experience South Indian food in a slightly elevated setting.
